findings.title: Possible KeyError and weak sender check when the integration has no sender
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is read directly. `build_integration` only stores `sender` if state has it, and the sender is set from the webhook. If the integration exists but the installation webhook has not populated `sender`, or `sender` has no `login`, this raises KeyError and the user gets a 500 instead of the error page. Use `.get()` and fail closed with `error()`. Also, the new check applies only when an Integration row already exists. On a fresh install (`Integration.DoesNotExist`, line 481-482) the authenticated user is never compared with anything, so the OAuth step adds no protection in that path.

findings.title: Token exchange request has no error handling and the redirect URI is built unsafely
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` is called outside the try block, so a network error or timeout raises and gives a 500. `get_user_info` is also unguarded. Separately, `state` and `redirect_uri` are put into the authorize URL without URL-encoding. The code also does not send `redirect_uri` or `state` in the token exchange, unlike the standard OAuth2 callback.

findings.title: installation_id taken from the request before the state is validated
findings.body: `OAuthLoginView` binds `installation_id` from `request.GET` into pipeline state before verifying `state` or the code. Any request carrying `installation_id` overwrites the stored value. `GitHubInstallation` then prefers `request.GET` over the stored state, so the value can still be replaced after OAuth. An attacker could therefore authenticate as themselves and then supply a different installation_id.

findings.title: Brittle assertion on call index and no tests for the new failure paths
findings.body: `responses.calls[2]` depends on the exact number of HTTP calls made by the new OAuth step. The PR also adds no tests for a state mismatch, a missing `access_token`, or a missing `login`, even though the description lists these as failure modes. The `test_installation_not_found` test now asserts the generic 'Invalid installation request.' message, which hides the original 404 'installation could not be found' behaviour.
